description: Residential bill anatomy at 1,000 kWh/month for large US utilities, assembled from tariffs/commission pages (2025-2026). See research/bills/FINDINGS.md.

categories.supply: generation/energy incl. capacity (default/standard-offer service in restructured states)
categories.base_energy: bundled base rate (generation+T+D) in vertically integrated utilities
categories.riders: surcharges/adjustment clauses (fuel, EE, storm, public-purpose, nuclear support, etc.)

how_it_reaches_bills: PJM runs the Base Residual Auction ~3 years ahead (recently compressed); each delivery year runs June 1 - May 31.
Load-serving entities pay the zonal clearing price x their customers' peak-load contribution; for default-service customers that cost is inside the supply/Price-to-Compare/SOS/BGS rate.

Restructured PJM states reset default-service prices on June 1 (PA, OH, IL, MD, NJ, DE, DC), so capacity changes show up in June bills; states that ladder procurement (NJ 3-year BGS, MD/DC/PA multi-year tranches) phase the change in over 2-3 years.
Shopping customers see it when their retail contract renews; vertically integrated PJM utilities (Dominion, APCo, many co-ops) recover capacity through base rates/riders instead of a June reset.

pjm_capacity_cost_cents_per_kwh_all_load.source: https://emp.lbl.gov/sites/default/files/2026-07/Retail%20Price%20Trends_2026%20edition_%20JulyUpdate_Data%20File.xlsx (tab: PJM capacity prices; from PJM IMM Q3-2025 State of the Market)

pjm_capacity_context.rule_of_thumb: At ~$330/MW-day, capacity is roughly 2 c/kWh averaged over all PJM load (~$20 on a 1,000 kWh bill); residential load is peakier than average, so the residential share can be higher. Pepco DC example: +1.7 c/kWh, +$10/mo (+9%) from the 2025/26 auction (Synapse for DC OPC).
